note: Adapted from the species description no. 276 in Chhotani (1997), Fauna of India: Isoptera. The original is in English; all three castes are present and the nymph is lacking. Synonymy lists, literature citations, figure numbers, distribution records and descriptions of wing microsculpture are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule oval, slightly longer than wide, widest at middle; antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 nearly equal to segments 3 and 4 combined, segment 4 shortest; labrum long, spear-shaped, reaching two-thirds of the mandibles, apex broader than in other species; mandibles thin and weak, apex slightly incurved; pronotum strongly saddle-shaped, anterior margin deeply concave. Alate with compound eyes round and protruding, very close to the lower margin of the head.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellow to yellowish brown; antennae cream-white; labrum light yellowish brown; body cream-white. Head and body rather densely pilose. Body length 3.2–5.0 mm. Head capsule oval, slightly longer than wide (0.80–1.0 mm to base of mandibles, maximum width 0.74–0.90 mm); widest at middle. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 2 nearly equal to segments 3 and 4 combined; segment 4 shortest. Labrum long, spear-shaped, reaching two-thirds of the mandibles; apex broader than in other species. Mandibles thin and weak, apex slightly incurved (0.49–0.55 mm long); slightly longer than half the head length (mandible length to head length ratio 0.55–0.62). Postmentum slightly longer than wide, slightly arched; sides slightly convex (0.40–0.59 mm long, 0.35–0.52 mm wide). Pronotum strongly saddle-shaped (0.33–0.50 mm long, 0.50–0.76 mm wide); anterior margin deeply concave, posterior margin slightly concave.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic. Major worker: head capsule yellow to yellowish brown; postclypeus slightly paler; antennae and body whitish. Head and body rather densely pilose. Body length 3.0–5.0 mm. Head subquadrate (0.80–0.90 mm to base of mandibles, maximum width 0.90–1.03 mm). Antennae 13–14-segmented; segment 2 equal to segments 3 and 4 combined. Postclypeus convex, about half as long as wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped (0.25–0.33 mm long, 0.45–0.50 mm wide). Minor worker: similar to major worker but smaller; body length 3.0–3.5 mm, head length to base of mandibles 0.60–0.65 mm, maximum head width 0.65–0.73 mm, pronotum width 0.35–0.43 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish brown to chestnut brown; antennae, labrum and postclypeus pale yellow; pronotum and abdominal tergites slightly paler than head capsule; wings brown. Head and body rather densely pilose. Body length with wings 14.0–16.0 mm, without wings 8.0–12.00 mm. Head capsule subcircular (0.92–1.15 mm to base of mandibles, maximum width including compound eyes 1.31–1.60 mm); ecdysial line not evident. Fontanelle a small round white spot. Compound eyes round, protruding (maximum diameter 0.35–0.48 mm, minimum diameter 0.30–0.36 mm); very close to the lower margin of the head, the distance less than one quarter of their short diameter. Ocellus large, oval (long diameter 0.15–0.28 mm, short diameter 0.10–0.16 mm); separated from compound eye by about half its short diameter (eye–ocellus distance 0.05–0.08 mm). Antennae 15–16-segmented; segments 2, 3 and 4 subequal in length, segment 2 sometimes slightly longer. Postclypeus strongly convex; length equal to half its width or slightly more. Pronotum subhemispherical, slightly narrower than head (0.68–0.98 mm long, maximum width 1.19–1.45 mm); anterior margin nearly straight, slightly raised, with a weak or indistinct notch at middle; posterior margin with a distinct notch. Wings long, sparsely pilose; forewing 12.0–12.5 mm long, hindwing 10.7–11.0 mm long.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Common species in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. It forms small subterranean colonies, constructing narrow galleries and chambers, or nests within the walls of nests of Odontotermes; the chambers contain fungus combs cultivated by the termites and also serve for brood rearing. It damages wheat seedlings, sugarcane, maize and the germinating seeds of some flowers and vegetables. In northern India, adults swarm from April to August.
